description: Gambling winnings of 1,500 to a resident payee: below both thresholds the publication states

source.quote: Gambling winnings of more than $5,000

why: Regular withholding applies only to gambling winnings of more than $5,000 (page 11), and page 2 states a 24% rule from $2,000 for bingo, slot machines and keno. 1,500 is below both, so the threshold hard rule gives 'do not withhold'. Page 12 adds that backup withholding at 24% applies to any gambling winnings when the payee gives no taxpayer identification number, which the query cannot tell: the answer is flagged for review. This case replaces two earlier ones at 4,999.99 and 5,000: between $2,000 and $5,000 the publication's two thresholds apply to different kinds of gambling that the closed payment_type vocabulary does not separate, so no single expected answer is defensible there. The threshold rule itself says 'certain kinds of gambling winnings', which adds condition_not_evaluable.

source.quote: Fijar en cincuenta y dos mil trescientos setenta y cuatro pesos ($52.374) el valor de la Unidad de Valor Tributario -UVT que regirá durante el año 2026

source.quote: para fijar el valor de la Unidad de Valor Tributario (UVT) aplicable para el año 2026.

why: $52.374 is the value of a unit of account, not a minimum payment for withholding, so the threshold hard rule must not fire and the answer stays unknown.
